chunks: 4672 - Hariz narrated from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
"Breastfeeding does not create prohibition except that which is compelled/established."
He said: I said, "What is meant by al-majbur?"
He said: "A mother who raises, or a wet nurse who is hired, or a bondwoman who is purchased."

key_terms.أُمٌّ: a mother caring for and nursing the child
key_terms.الرَّضَاعِ: breastfeeding or suckling that may establish milk kinship
key_terms.ظِئْرٌ: a wet nurse employed to suckle a child
key_terms.مَجْبُورًا: established in a binding, committed nursing arrangement
key_terms.يَحْرُمُ: becomes prohibited in marriage due to legal effect

ai.seo_question: When does breastfeeding establish marriage prohibition in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on milk kinship, stating that prohibition through breastfeeding is established only in a recognized, committed nursing arrangement. The Imam عليه السلام explains this through examples such as a mother raising the child, a hired wet nurse, or a bondwoman purchased for that purpose.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4672 - Hariz narrated from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:
"Breastfeeding does not create a prohibition except when it is continuous and intentional."
I asked: "What is meant by continuous and intentional?"
Imam (as) replied: "It is when a mother raises the child, a wet nurse is hired, or a bondwoman is purchased for breastfeeding."
